results.contract: The engine serves Bootstrap 5.3.8's alert data API (delegated `[data-bs-dismiss="alert"]` clicks resolving `data-bs-target`, `href`, or the closest `.alert`), the `close` method, and the cancelable `close.bs.alert` and `closed.bs.alert` events on Bootstrap's own markup. It does this through the `createAlert` factory and the `createAlertPlugin` route rather than Bootstrap's static class API, as /home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:616, :622, :634, :636, and :648 state, with the deliberate differences recorded in the "Engine departures" table at /home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:716-748.

behaviors.title: should take care of element either passed as a CSS selector or DOM element
behaviors.evidence: The engine's factory takes a host element only: /home/user/veneer/src/browser/factories.ts:226 `createAlert(element: HTMLElement, ...)`, and guide /home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:622 says 'A factory takes Bootstrap's host element'. Bootstrap's constructor API is not part of what guide :616 serves (data API, plugin methods, events).

behaviors.title: should return version
behaviors.evidence: src/browser exposes no static VERSION (a grep for VERSION under /home/user/veneer/src/browser returns nothing). The served surface at /home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:616 and :622 is the data API, factories, and events, not Bootstrap's class statics.

behaviors.title: DATA_KEY: should return plugin data key
behaviors.evidence: DATA_KEY `bs.alert` is Bootstrap's internal Data map key (js/src/base-component.js:73-75). The engine keys its registry by plugin name `alert` (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/plugins.ts:35, guide /home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:620,622).

behaviors.title: data-api: should close an alert without instantiating it manually
behaviors.evidence: /home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/plugins.test.ts:25 (lines 58 and 61-66): the alert route builds the component on an uninstantiated host and removes it (`!host.isConnected`). The oracle cases are /home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Alert.test.ts:82 (button click, fade false and true, comparison empty) and :318 (a click builds the markup-only alert). The oracle helper pre-creates the component through createAlert at Alert.test.ts:45 before the click, so the oracle never compares the route-construction path (see questions).

The engine aborts the second pending wait in destroy (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/Alert.ts:64), while Bootstrap's second transitionend handler throws a TypeError. Add an oracle case for two clicks during the fade plus a departure row for the error count.
behaviors.evidence: No Alert.test.ts case drives two closes before completion (/home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Alert.test.ts:82-343), and no alert row exists beyond /home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:747-748.

behaviors.title: Dismiss delegation phase: Bootstrap listens in the document bubble phase, the engine in the document capture phase
behaviors.claim: A page stopPropagation on the trigger or an ancestor blocks Bootstrap's dismissal but not the engine's, and close.bs.alert precedes the page's own trigger click listeners in the engine but follows them in Bootstrap. /home/user/veneer/src/browser/Veneer.ts:70-73 must route in the bubble phase, or the guide must carry a departure row consumed by an oracle case.
behaviors.evidence: Capture is deliberate (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/Veneer.ts:71; guide /home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:618; engine-only proof at /home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Veneer.test.ts:635-637). No row in /home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:720-988 names the phase, and no alert oracle case stops propagation.

behaviors.title: Orphan or unresolvable dismiss trigger: Bootstrap throws (TypeError on a null instance, or SyntaxError on an invalid selector); the engine does nothing or falls back to the closest .alert
behaviors.claim: With an invalid data-bs-target, /home/user/veneer/src/browser/helpers.ts:715-723 returns [] and /home/user/veneer/src/browser/helpers.ts:187 then dismisses the ancestor alert, where Bootstrap throws and leaves it. With no target and no ancestor, the engine does nothing where Bootstrap throws. The engine must match Bootstrap, or the guide must record a row with a proof.
behaviors.evidence: There is no proof in /home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Alert.test.ts or /home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/helpers.test.ts:377-402 for an invalid or unmatched target with an alert ancestor, and no departure row.

questions: The oracle helper compareAlert creates the engine alert through createAlert (/home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Alert.test.ts:45-51) before every data-API click, while the Bootstrap frame builds its instance on the click. The oracle therefore never compares the route-construction path that spec alert.spec.js:38 pins; only the non-oracle /home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/plugins.test.ts:61-66 covers it. Should the data-API oracle cases run without the factory call, attaching the veto listener on the host instead? Referred to the Orchestrator.

Guide /home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:618 states capture-phase routing as contract, but the departure table (:720-988) has no row for the phase difference against Bootstrap's bubble-phase document delegation. Is this a missing row or an engine defect? This is a subjective and contract ruling for the Orchestrator.

Several error-only differences have no row: close after completion or destroy, a second close during the fade, destroy inside a close.bs.alert listener, and an orphan or invalid-selector dismiss trigger. Should each get a supplemental `$::errors` row like alert-destroy (/home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:747), or should one shared row record that the engine refuses Bootstrap's null-host TypeErrors?

The guide does not name Bootstrap's static class API (VERSION, DATA_KEY, getInstance, getOrCreateInstance, and a selector-string constructor) as refused. The out-of-contract rulings here rely on /home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:616 and :622 describing the served surface. Should the Browser entry chapter name that refusal explicitly?

results.contract: The engine serves Bootstrap's button data API (a delegated click on `[data-bs-toggle="button"]` that prevents default and toggles class `active` with a matching `aria-pressed`), the `toggle` method, and creation or lookup through `createButton`, `createButtonPlugin`, and `Registry.component`, all on Bootstrap's markup. A scope must opt in to this (/home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:616-622), and `destroy` plus the Veneer-only `toggle.vn.button` notification come from /home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:634-636. The departure table at /home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:716-764 records the notification as the button family's only rows, and /home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:648 describes the button proofs.

No departure row records the renames. Should line 616 narrow its claim, or should the table carry an API-vocabulary row?

results.contract: The engine serves Bootstrap 5.3.8's collapse data API (the `[data-bs-toggle="collapse"]` click route with anchor prevention and `{ toggle: false }` construction, plugins.ts:110-126), the show/hide/toggle methods with `*.bs.collapse` events, and a `createCollapse` factory plus `Registry.component` in place of Bootstrap's class, constructor, statics, and jQuery interface (guides/veneer.md:616, :622, :634, :638). Every deliberate difference must be a row of the Engine departures table (guides/veneer.md:718). The collapse rows are guides/veneer.md:859-872 and :986, plus the shared rows at :742-744.

results.contract: The engine serves Bootstrap 5.3.8's carousel data API, the `createCarousel` factory, and the `slide.bs.carousel` and `slid.bs.carousel` events. The data API covers the gated click on `[data-bs-slide], [data-bs-slide-to]` and load boot of `[data-bs-ride="carousel"]`, and the factory exposes `next`, `previous`, `select`, `start`, `pause`, `resume`, and `destroy`; Swipe is the gesture utility (guides/veneer.md:616, 618, 622, 634, 636, 656, 662). The deliberate differences are the carousel-pause, carousel-destroy, and carousel-destroyed departure rows at guides/veneer.md:904-942, plus the shared event-detail, transition-wait, and registry-plugins rows at :742-745.

questions: Orchestrator: guides/veneer.md:616 and :622 frame the contract as the data API, plugin methods, events, and factories. No sentence says the engine does not serve Bootstrap's class statics (VERSION, DATA_KEY, Default as a class static, a CSS-selector constructor argument, getInstance). Should the Browser entry chapter state that refusal explicitly so that the out-of-contract rulings rest on a cited line?

Orchestrator: three destroy-time differences show only in engine-only assertions (tests/src/browser/Carousel.test.ts:252-253, 247-248), and a fourth only in an oracle-only error count (:349). Each departs from Bootstrap 5.3.8: pointer-event class removal, dragstart release, touch-timeout cancellation, and the post-dispose TypeError. The departure-table preamble (guides/veneer.md:718) requires a row for every deliberate difference, and the guide's prose (:656, :662) describes only the first two. Should these become ledger rows consumed under touch emulation, matching the alert-destroy $::errors row at :747?

Swipe.ts:48-65 (the path for a realm without PointerEvent: touchstart, touchmove, touchend, and pinch) is never executed by any proof because Chromium always exposes PointerEvent. Is a stubbed-realm case wanted, or is that path to be declared outside the proven contract?

The engine reads the active item from classes after a slide completes (src/browser/Carousel.ts:168-172). Bootstrap keeps a stale _activeElement after completion (carousel.js:289, 342). The two diverge only when page code moves the active class between slides; no case or row covers it. Is it to be recorded or ruled out of contract?

results.contract: The engine serves Bootstrap 5.3.8's dropdown data API (delegated toggle click and toggle/menu keydown in the capture phase, then bubble-phase clearing on document click and keyup), the show/hide/toggle/update/destroy methods plus `dismiss(event)`, the `*.bs.dropdown` events with typed detail, and `createDropdown` for factory access. The scope sits in /home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:616 (what the engine serves), :618 (clearing only through a scope that includes the dropdown plugin, so a page that uses factories alone gets no outside clearing), :622 (factory and registry lifetime), :634 (the members and the `DROPDOWN_MENU` refusal), and :638 (grouped options, with function inputs and Popper callbacks refused); every deliberate difference is a row under "### Engine departures" at :716-988.

questions: Refer to Orchestrator: guide:718 says the table records every deliberate difference, but three differences appear only in prose and have no row. (1) guide:618: there is no outside clearing for a page that uses factories alone. (2) guide:622: a factory call with options destroys and rebuilds a lifetime built from markup alone, where Bootstrap's getOrCreateInstance ignores the config. (3) guide:634: VeneerError DROPDOWN_MENU where Bootstrap throws a TypeError. Should each get a row?

Refer to subjective lane: guide:654 says the dropdown proofs compare the offset, boundary, and reference inputs through the data API. Dropdown.test.ts:631-635 drops every style reading, the fixture neither overflows nor flips, and the Placement population cases bypass Dropdown.ts:117-128. Should the guide claim be narrowed, or should the case compare rendered boxes through createDropdown?

Refer to subjective lane: guide:60 says DROPDOWN_DEFAULTS supplies Bootstrap's dropdown option defaults, but src/browser/constants.ts:86-90 has only distance, display, and reference (no autoClose, boundary, skid, or popperConfig).

Refer to subjective lane: the Dropdown.placement getter (Dropdown.ts:82) reaches Placement.placement, which writes data-popper-placement (Placement.ts:133-134), so reading the getter writes to the DOM.

Orchestrator ruling needed: a virtual-element reference (spec:537) has no type, no row, and no refusal in guide:638. Should the engine support it (anchor positioning needs an element), or should a departure row record it?

results.contract: The engine serves Bootstrap 5.3.8's modal data API (`[data-bs-toggle="modal"]` and `[data-bs-dismiss="modal"]`), the `show`, `shown`, `hide`, `hidden`, and `hidePrevented.bs.modal` events, and the `createModal` factory with show, hide, toggle, update, and destroy on Bootstrap's own markup; `Backdrop`, `Trap`, `Lock`, and `Hold` are its shared mechanics (/home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:616, 622, 634, 640, 652). Deliberate differences are the trap-owner, lock-priority, saved-attributes, overlapping-locks, modal:overlap, and modal:destroy opening rows of the Engine departures table (/home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:716-844), and jQuery and Bootstrap's class statics fall outside that contract.

behaviors.title: VERSION: should return plugin version
behaviors.evidence: The engine exposes no class statics. A factory takes the host element and returns its live component (guides/veneer.md:622), and the method vocabulary is guides/veneer.md:634.

behaviors.title: Default: should return plugin default config
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/helpers.test.ts:650 compares Bootstrap's `_getConfig` merge with `resolveModalOptions` on identical markup; tests/src/browser/helpers.test.ts:686-707 checks how defaults are projected.

behaviors.title: DATA_KEY: should return plugin data key
behaviors.evidence: This is Bootstrap's internal data-store key. The engine registry is keyed by host and plugin (guides/veneer.md:622; departure row registry-plugins at guides/veneer.md:745).

behaviors.title: constructor: should take care of element either passed as a CSS selector or DOM element
behaviors.evidence: Per guides/veneer.md:622, a factory takes Bootstrap's host element; the engine accepts no selector strings.

behaviors.title: toggle: should call ScrollBarHelper to handle scrollBar on body
behaviors.evidence: In tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:286 ('saved overflow', 'fixed and sticky', and 'methods'), the oracle compares the body overflow, padding, and data-bs-* writes on show and hide. Modal.ts:121 acquires the lock and Modal.ts:227 releases it.

behaviors.title: show: should show a modal
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:213 runs an oracle transcript that records aria-modal, role, aria-hidden, style, and the added backdrop. The aria-modal, class, style, and added[0] instruments have controls at Modal.test.ts:251-273.

behaviors.title: show: should show a modal without backdrop
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/factories.test.ts:187-208 passes dismiss.backdrop false, reaches phase shown, and finds no `.modal-backdrop`.

behaviors.title: show: should show a modal and append the element
behaviors.claim: When the host is detached, show must append it to the body before the display write (src/browser/Modal.ts:196). No proof shows a detached host.
behaviors.evidence: No case in tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts or elsewhere under tests/ builds a detached modal host; a grep for dynamic or detached modal fixtures finds none.

behaviors.title: show: should do nothing if a modal is shown
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:143 (fade false) runs toggle and toggle against the oracle. A visible guard that ignored the show class would emit a second show event, and the oracle comparison would fail (Modal.ts:97-103, 117).

behaviors.title: show: should do nothing if a modal is transitioning
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/factories.test.ts:203-207 calls show twice while showing and gets open.count 1.

behaviors.title: show: should not fire shown event when show is prevented
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:293 'show veto' runs the oracle with a prevented show.bs.modal (steps at Modal.test.ts:348-350 and 394-398).

behaviors.title: show: should be shown after the first call to show() has been prevented while fading is enabled
behaviors.claim: A vetoed show on a fade modal must leave no state that refuses the next show (src/browser/Modal.ts:117-120). No proof retries show after a veto.
behaviors.evidence: The 'show veto' case (tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:348-350) ends after the vetoed open, and no other modal case calls show again after a prevented show.

behaviors.title: show: should set is transitioning if fade class is present
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:537-538 shows phase 'showing' after show() on a fade modal, and tests/src/browser/factories.test.ts:205 waits for phase 'shown'.

behaviors.title: show: should close modal when a click occurred on data-bs-dismiss="modal" inside modal
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:219-221 clicks .btn-close until hidden.bs.modal and compares the result with the oracle.

behaviors.title: show: should close modal when a click occurred on a data-bs-dismiss="modal" with "bs-target" outside of modal element
behaviors.evidence: In tests/src/browser/plugins.test.ts:44-66, a dismiss trigger outside the host with data-bs-target resolves and builds the target modal. If resolveDismiss ignored targets (helpers.ts:185-186), the host would not be resolved and the case would fail.

behaviors.title: show: should set .modal's scroll top to 0
behaviors.claim: show must reset the host's scrollTop to 0 (src/browser/Modal.ts:201). A proof must scroll the host before a reopen and compare the reading with the oracle.
behaviors.evidence: The oracle records scroll position (guides/veneer.md:646), but every modal case opens a host that has never been scrolled. Deleting Modal.ts:201 would therefore change no reading.

behaviors.title: show: should set modal body scroll top to 0 if modal body do not exists
behaviors.claim: show must reset `.modal-body` scrollTop to 0 (src/browser/Modal.ts:202-203). A proof needs a scrolled `.modal-body` fixture.
behaviors.evidence: buildModal (tests/setupBrowser.ts:4259-4275) has no `.modal-body`, and no modal case adds one.

behaviors.title: show: should not trap focus if focus equal to false
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:288 'focus disabled' sets data-bs-focus=false (line 312) and focuses #opener (line 364), and the focus reading is compared with the oracle.

behaviors.title: show: should add listener when escape touch is pressed
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Veneer.test.ts:848-885 presses Escape inside an open modal with keyboard true in both realms, and the dialog hides identically (readings at 872-882).

behaviors.title: show: should do nothing when the pressed key is not escape
behaviors.evidence: The 'tab:shown' row (tests/setupBrowser.ts:3035, from shown to shown) is driven by tests/app/browser/integration.test.ts:1162. If the key check at Modal.ts:58 were removed, Tab would hide the modal.

behaviors.title: show: should adjust dialog on resize
behaviors.claim: A window resize while the modal is shown and settled must rerun the dialog adjustment (src/browser/Modal.ts:79-85). No proof dispatches resize to a shown modal.
behaviors.evidence: A grep for resize in tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts finds nothing. 'resize.bs.modal' in ORACLE_EVENTS (tests/setupBrowser.ts:4183) is a handler namespace that Bootstrap never dispatches as a native event.

behaviors.title: show: should not close modal when clicking on modal-content
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Veneer.test.ts:862-882 clicks controls inside the modal content in both realms, and the dialog stays shown identically. The 'drag out' case (Modal.test.ts:291, 412-417, 462-466) pins the down-target check.

behaviors.title: show: should not close modal when clicking outside of modal-content if backdrop = false
behaviors.claim: With dismiss.backdrop false, a mousedown and click on the host must not hide the modal (src/browser/Modal.ts:71-72). No proof clicks the host of a backdrop-less modal.
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/factories.test.ts:187-213 uses backdrop false but never clicks the host. The Modal.test.ts:286 scenarios have no backdrop-false case.

behaviors.title: show: should not close modal when clicking outside of modal-content if backdrop = static
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:289 'static backdrop' clicks #modal until hidePrevented, settles, and compares the result with the oracle (lines 313, 353-357).

behaviors.title: show: should close modal when escape key is pressed with keyboard = true and backdrop is static
behaviors.claim: Escape must hide a modal that has a static backdrop and keyboard true (src/browser/Modal.ts:58-60). No proof presses Escape on a static modal whose keyboard option is true.
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/helpers.test.ts:650-664 pins only the option projection (dismiss.escape true). The 'Escape refused' case sets keyboard false (Modal.test.ts:314-317), and the showcase static dialog refuses Escape (tests/setupBrowser.ts:3047).

behaviors.title: show: should not close modal when escape key is pressed with keyboard = false
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:290 'Escape refused' presses Escape until hidePrevented and compares the result with the oracle (lines 314-317, 358-362).

behaviors.title: show: should not overflow when clicking outside of modal-content if backdrop = static
behaviors.evidence: In tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:289 'static backdrop', the settle step lets the oracle compare the overflow-y write and its restoration. tests/setupBrowser.test.ts:627 also records the modal-static bounce.

behaviors.title: show: should not queue multiple callbacks when clicking outside of modal-content and backdrop = static
behaviors.claim: A second refused dismissal during a running bounce must not start another bounce (src/browser/Modal.ts:236-240). No proof sends two refused clicks.
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:353-357 and tests/setupBrowser.test.ts:627-650 each send a single refused click or Escape.

behaviors.title: show: should trap focus
behaviors.evidence: In tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:300 'trap', the focus step to #opener (line 365) runs while the modal is shown, and the oracle compares where focus settles.

behaviors.title: hide: should hide a modal
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:213 runs the oracle transcript through hidden.bs.modal, covering aria-hidden, aria-modal, role, display none, and backdrop removal.

behaviors.title: hide: should close modal when clicking outside of modal-content
behaviors.evidence: In tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:291 'drag out', a mousedown on the dialog followed by a click on the host does not close the modal (oracle-compared). The 'backdrop:shown' row for the archive dialog (tests/setupBrowser.ts:3044, from shown to hidden) is driven by tests/app/browser/integration.test.ts:1162.

behaviors.title: hide: should not close modal when clicking on an element removed from modal content
behaviors.claim: A click whose target is a descendant removed during the click must not hide the modal, even after a mousedown on the host (src/browser/Modal.ts:70). No proof covers it.
behaviors.evidence: No case under tests/src/browser removes a clicked element inside a modal.

behaviors.title: hide: should do nothing is the modal is not shown
behaviors.claim: hide on a hidden modal must emit no hide or hidden event and make no writes (src/browser/Modal.ts:129). No proof asserts events or writes after a hide on a hidden modal.
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/plugins.test.ts:61-66 runs the dismiss route on a hidden modal but asserts only that the registry entry exists. If the `!this.visible` guard were removed, that case would still pass.

behaviors.title: hide: should do nothing is the modal is transitioning
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:143 (fade true) calls show() and then hide() in the same task, and the oracle records only show and shown (lines 185-189).

behaviors.title: hide: should not hide a modal if hide is prevented
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:294 'hide veto' compares with the oracle (lines 394-398, 439-443). tests/src/browser/factories.test.ts:209-210 checks that the phase stays shown.

behaviors.title: hide: should release focus trap
behaviors.claim: hide must deactivate the modal's trap when the hide starts (src/browser/Modal.ts:132). A proof must move focus outside during the hide transition, or must check `Trap.active` after hide.
behaviors.evidence: The 'trap' case (Modal.test.ts:300) and the trap-owner checkpoints (tests/setupBrowser.ts:3757-3786) read focus only after display none, when a trap that was not released cannot pull focus anyway. Removing Modal.ts:132 would change no reading.

behaviors.title: dispose: should dispose a modal
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:529-546 checks registry release and that the lock and backdrop are gone. Modal.test.ts:50-86 shows the trap released on destroy, and factories.test.ts:217-220 shows that show after destroy does nothing.

behaviors.title: handleUpdate: should call adjust dialog
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:292 'overflow' calls update and compares the result with Bootstrap's handleUpdate (lines 366-367, 405-408, 456-459).

behaviors.title: data-api: should toggle modal
behaviors.claim: A second click on the toggle of an open modal must run Bootstrap's hide-then-toggle sequence: a non-fade modal hides and reopens, and a fade modal stays hiding (src/browser/plugins.ts:212-218 through helpers.ts:840-841). No proof clicks the toggle of an already-open modal.
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:213 opens with the toggle and closes with .btn-close. The 'overlap' case (Modal.test.ts:368-371) hides a different modal, so a mutation that skips previous.hide() when previous is the component would not be detected.

behaviors.title: data-api: should not recreate a new modal
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:122-124 creates the modal by click, and createModal then returns that live component (phase shown). tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:564-569 adds further checks.

behaviors.title: data-api: should prevent default when the trigger is <a> or <area>
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:26-42 checks that an anchor toggle click has defaultPrevented true in both realms (fallback at helpers.ts:94-98).

behaviors.title: data-api: should focus the trigger on hide
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:213 opens with the data API and closes, and the oracle compares the focus reading. A control on the focus instrument is at lines 251-273.

behaviors.title: data-api: should open modal, having special characters in its id
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/helpers.test.ts:955-961 resolves `#42:panel` through CSS.escape (helpers.ts:716-720).

behaviors.title: data-api: should not prevent default when a click occurred on data-bs-dismiss="modal" where tagName is DIFFERENT than <a> or <area>
behaviors.claim: A click on a button dismiss must stay unprevented (src/browser/helpers.ts:94-98). No proof reads defaultPrevented for a non-anchor dismiss click.
behaviors.evidence: ORACLE_EVENTS has no native click, and its 'click.dismiss.bs.modal' entry never fires (tests/setupBrowser.ts:4162). helpers.test.ts:154-184 covers only an explicit predicate.

behaviors.title: data-api: should prevent default when a click occurred on data-bs-dismiss="modal" where tagName is <a> or <area>
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/plugins.test.ts:55-57 checks that an anchor dismiss click is prevented before the disabled refusal.

behaviors.title: data-api: should not focus the trigger if the modal is not visible
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/helpers.test.ts:1357-1360 sets trigger.hidden, and the trigger is not focused after close (restoreFocus at helpers.ts:860).

behaviors.title: data-api: should not focus the trigger if the modal is not shown
behaviors.claim: A prevented show.bs.modal must disarm focus restoration for that trigger (src/browser/helpers.ts:831-838). No proof dispatches a prevented show.
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/helpers.test.ts:1342-1346 dispatches only an unprevented `new Event('show.bs.modal')`, so removing the defaultPrevented check at helpers.ts:835 would not be detected.

behaviors.title: data-api: should call hide first, if another modal is open
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:296 'overlap' (#next click, lines 368-371) is compared with the oracle under the modal:overlap rows. tests/src/browser/helpers.test.ts:1339-1340 covers the same path.

behaviors.evidence: The dispatch puts jQuery interop outside the contract; modal.js:318-332 is jQueryInterface.

behaviors.evidence: jQuery interop is outside the contract (dispatch).

behaviors.title: jQueryInterface: should throw error on undefined method
behaviors.evidence: jQuery interop is outside the contract (dispatch).

behaviors.title: getInstance: should return modal instance
behaviors.evidence: The engine equivalent is the factory and registry lookup (guides/veneer.md:622). tests/src/browser/factories.test.ts:201 checks that factory(element) returns the component.

behaviors.title: getInstance: should return null when there is no modal instance
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Veneer.test.ts:907-912 checks that Registry.component returns undefined for an unbuilt host.

behaviors.title: getOrCreateInstance: should return modal instance

behaviors.title: getOrCreateInstance: should return new instance when there is no modal instance

behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:566-572 checks that a later call returns the configured component and ignores its options (rule at guides/veneer.md:622).

behaviors.title: show: should append the backdrop html once on show and include the "show" class if it is "shown"
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Backdrop.test.ts:9-29 checks that the class is ["modal-backdrop","show"] and equals the oracle's className. A single node is reused (Backdrop.ts:42-56).

behaviors.title: show: should not append the backdrop html if it is not "shown"
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Backdrop.test.ts:64-70 shows that `enabled: false` creates no element.

behaviors.title: show: should append the backdrop html once and include the "fade" class if it is "shown" and "animated"
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:213 (fade modal) records the added backdrop's classes against the oracle. The rows at guides/veneer.md:772-774 show ["fade","modal-backdrop","show"].

behaviors.title: hide: should remove the backdrop html
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Backdrop.test.ts:34-35 checks node.isConnected false after hide.

behaviors.title: hide: should remove the "show" class
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:213 records the backdrop's class write before removal, compared with the oracle.

behaviors.title: hide: should not try to remove Node on remove method if it is not "shown"
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/factories.test.ts:209-213 hides a backdrop-less modal to phase hidden. If the guard at Backdrop.ts:66 were removed, an unhandled rejection would fail the run.

behaviors.title: hide: should not error if the backdrop no longer has a parent
behaviors.claim: Backdrop.hide must resolve without error when its root was detached while shown (src/browser/Backdrop.ts:65-76). Offcanvas roots its backdrop at the panel's parent (Offcanvas.ts:49), so a detached root can occur.
behaviors.evidence: No case in tests/src/browser/Backdrop.test.ts detaches the root before hide.

behaviors.title: click callback: should execute callback on click
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Backdrop.test.ts:30-40 checks that mousedown calls the callback, click does not, and nothing fires after removal.

behaviors.title: animation callbacks: should show and hide backdrop after counting transition duration if it is animated
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:299 'destroy opening' sets a 1s backdrop transition (lines 326-327) and destroys before the wait completes. If the engine skipped the wait, the dialog writes would appear outside the modal:destroy opening rows and the case would fail.

behaviors.title: animation callbacks: should show and hide backdrop without a delay if it is not animated
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:143 (fade false) requires show, shown, hide, and hidden in one task, matching the oracle (lines 185-189).

behaviors.title: animation callbacks: should not call delay callbacks if it is not "shown"
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Backdrop.test.ts:64-70 checks that a disabled backdrop resolves without creating a node or waiting (Backdrop.ts:37).

behaviors.title: Config rootElement: should be appended on "document.body" by default
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:213 records the added backdrop under the body ('$'), and the parent '$' appears in the rows at guides/veneer.md:772.

behaviors.title: Config rootElement: should find the rootElement if passed as a string
behaviors.evidence: This is Bootstrap's internal string config: modal.js:158-163 never passes rootElement, and the engine's BackdropOptions.root takes an element (Backdrop.ts:41).

behaviors.title: Config rootElement: should be appended on any element given by the proper config
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Backdrop.test.ts:12-29 uses `root` as a section element.

behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Lock.test.ts:148-153 checks width > 0 with a 2600px body in classic mode (Lock.ts:30-38).

behaviors.title: isBodyOverflowing: should return false if body is not overflowing

behaviors.title: getWidth: should return an integer greater than zero, if body is overflowing
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Lock.test.ts:151-165 checks width > 0 and the compensations `${width+3}px`, `${width+7}px`, and `${9-width}px`.

behaviors.title: getWidth: should return 0 if body is not overflowing
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:286 oracle comparison of body padding on pages without a scrollbar.

behaviors.title: hide - reset: should adjust the inline padding of fixed elements which are full-width
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Lock.test.ts:143-164, 223 covers this, and tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:298 'fixed and sticky' compares it with the oracle (fixtures at lines 333-342).

behaviors.evidence: Lock restores through Hold (Lock.ts:115-116, 97), and tests/src/browser/Hold.test.ts:91-108 checks that an absent style is removed on release.

behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Lock.test.ts:165, 224 checks the sticky margin, and tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:298 compares it with the oracle.

behaviors.title: hide - reset: should not adjust the inline margin and padding of sticky and fixed elements when element do not have full width

behaviors.title: Body Handling: should hide scrollbar and reset it to its initial value
behaviors.evidence: tests/src/browser/Lock.test.ts:82-107 compares padding and saved-attribute values with the oracle; Lock.test.ts:108-137 compares the order of saved overflow writes.

behaviors.title: Body Handling: should hide scrollbar and reset it to its initial value - respecting css rules
behaviors.claim: When body padding comes only from a stylesheet, the lock must add the width to the computed value and write no data-bs-padding-right (src/browser/Lock.ts:75, 117). No proof uses stylesheet padding.

questions: Orchestrator: Modal.update reads Lock.width (src/browser/Modal.ts:151 through src/browser/Lock.ts:30-33), which is the first owner's measurement taken before the lock. Bootstrap's _adjustDialog measures after the lock (js/src/modal.js:118, 298). On a page whose body overflow reaches the viewport, that measurement is 0. My reading is that, with classic scrollbars, the engine writes padding-right on a short modal where Bootstrap writes none. No modal oracle case runs with a page scrollbar (tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:430-438 moves the body contents out). Rule whether update must measure afresh or whether this needs a departure row.

Objective lane: ORACLE_EVENTS (tests/setupBrowser.ts:4153-4184) lists handler namespaces such as 'click.dismiss.bs.modal', 'keydown.dismiss.bs.modal', 'mousedown.bs.backdrop', 'focusin.bs.focustrap', 'resize.bs.modal', and 'click.bs.modal.data-api'. Bootstrap's EventHandler registers these on native click, keydown, mousedown, and resize, and never dispatches them under those names, so the capture listeners at tests/setupBrowser.ts:4832 cannot fire for them. guides/veneer.md:646 says the list bounds the instrument; those entries record nothing. Confirm, and decide whether to remove them or replace them with native readings such as the click defaultPrevented value.

Subjective lane: guides/veneer.md:616 says the engine serves Bootstrap's plugin methods, yet handleUpdate is renamed update, dispose is renamed destroy, and getInstance and getOrCreateInstance are replaced by the factory and registry. The factory also replaces a markup-built component when given options (guides/veneer.md:622), where Bootstrap's getOrCreateInstance ignores the config. None of these is a row in the Engine departures table (guides/veneer.md:718 claims that table records every deliberate difference). Rule whether line 718 scopes the table to markup only or whether rows are needed.

Objective lane: the 'overflow' case appends the 2000px content before show (tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:318-321), so show() already writes the same padding that the later update step (Modal.test.ts:366-367) would write. If update() alone became a no-op once the modal is shown, no reading would change. Consider growing the content after shown and before update.

results.contract: The engine serves Bootstrap 5.3.8's popover on Bootstrap's own markup and data-bs-* attributes. It does this through the `Tip<'popover'>` profile, which supplies the `createPopover` factory, the opt-in `createPopoverPlugin({ boot: true })`, the show, hide, toggle, enable, disable, update, write, and destroy methods, and the `*.bs.popover` events. It serves no Bootstrap class statics, no jQuery plugin, and no function-valued config; guide /home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:616, :622, :624-630, and :638 state this contract, and the departure table at :716-988 records each deliberate difference.

behaviors.claim: The engine must keep an accepted open state and its scroll lock when `show()` supersedes a pending `hide()`; this belongs in /home/user/veneer/src/browser/Offcanvas.ts. In the engine, `#lock.acquire()` is a no-op for the owner that still holds the lock (Lock.ts:46). The stale `#close` then releases the lock and removes aria-modal and role (Offcanvas.ts:186-188), so `visible` derives false (:94-101). Escape, backdrop, and dismiss then call `hide()` and do nothing (:133). Bootstrap keeps `_isShown` true and the body locked, so Escape still closes. Add an oracle scenario: open through the data API, click `.btn-close`, then click #opener before `hidden`.
behaviors.evidence: Bootstrap re-saves overflow at scrollbar.js:60, :79-83, and its hide completion restores 'hidden' (:86-96), so the body stays locked. Its toggle and hide gate on `_isShown` (offcanvas.js:90, :129). No case in /home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Offcanvas.test.ts:193-210 drives hide followed by show. Backdrop.show also aborts the pending removal (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/Backdrop.ts:38), where Bootstrap's pending dispose removes the backdrop (backdrop.js:93-95). That difference has no departure row.

questions: Orchestrator: the guide states the served surface (/home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:616, :622, :634) but never refuses Bootstrap's static class API (VERSION, DATA_KEY, Default, getInstance, getOrCreateInstance, and dispose renamed to destroy). Does the guide need a refusal sentence, so that the out-of-contract rulings on VERSION and DATA_KEY rest on stated text and not on omission?

Orchestrator: no departure row names destroy of a settled shown panel. The engine releases the body lock and removes show, aria-modal, and role (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/Offcanvas.ts:153-168), while Bootstrap's dispose leaves all of them. The guide says every deliberate difference is a row (:718), but only the 'destroy closing' scenario is compared (:845-858). Is a 'destroy shown' scenario with rows required?

Objective lane: the re-show-during-hide finding comes from reading Offcanvas.ts:115-191, Lock.ts:45-46, and :92-103, and Bootstrap's scrollbar.js:37-96. A browser run needs to confirm which of `#close` and `#open` settles first under `awaitTransition`. Either order ends with `visible` false and the lock released. If `#open` settles first, the backdrop also stays shown over a hidden panel and its mousedown does nothing.

results.contract: The engine serves Bootstrap 5.3.8's scrollspy on Bootstrap's markup: it boots `[data-bs-spy="scroll"]` through an opted-in `createVeneer` scope, keeps the intersection algorithm and the `active` writes on links and their parents, dispatches `activate.bs.scrollspy` with the legacy `relatedTarget`, and offers `createScrollspy` with typed options, `refresh`, `destroy`, and `current` in place of Bootstrap's class statics and jQuery plugin (/home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:616, :618, :622, :634, :658). The one scrollspy departure row is `scrollspy:detail`, typed activation detail (/home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:738), plus the shared `mistyped-input` and `event-detail` rows (:739, :742).

results.contract: The engine serves Bootstrap 5.3.8's tooltip on Bootstrap's markup through the opt-in tooltip plugin and `createTooltip(element, options)`. It uses the TooltipInterface vocabulary (show, hide, toggle, enable, disable, update, write, destroy, with the getters enabled, panel, placement, visible, and phase), the TIP_EVENTS hooks, and the show/inserted/shown/hide/hidden `.bs.tooltip` events (guide/veneer.md:616, :622-634, :444-455). Markup input reads `data-bs-*` attributes but not `data-bs-config` or the sanitizer keys, and a function-valued input resolves to its default. Placement replaces Popper, and every deliberate difference is a row of the departure table at guide/veneer.md:716-988 (see :638 and :644).

behaviors.title: setContent on a shown tip disposes it before a refused re-show
behaviors.evidence: Bootstrap's setContent calls _disposePopper before show(), so a show veto, disable(), an emptied title, a detached host, or inline display:none removes the tip, with no hidden event. Engine write (src/browser/Tip.ts:259-265) calls show(), which returns or throws at :152-164 before #disposePanel, so the old panel stays shown with old content. Example: tip.show(); tip.disable(); tip.write({title:'Copied'}) leaves Bootstrap with no .tooltip and the engine with a visible panel. No row and no case.
behaviors.claim: Tip.write on a visible tip must release the current panel before calling show(), as Bootstrap's setContent does, or record each refusal path as a departure row. The aria-describedby outcome also needs a row, because Bootstrap leaves the stale id.

behaviors.title: SVG relatedTarget and target inside the trigger
behaviors.evidence: Bootstrap's mouseenter/leave wrapper skips any Node relatedTarget inside the delegateTarget. Its delegation walks parentNode from any target. The engine accepts only HTMLElement (src/browser/validators.ts:11-20) at src/browser/Tip.ts:351 and :378-382. Moving the pointer from <a> onto its inline <svg> fires mouseout with an SVG relatedTarget: the engine runs #leave and hides, and the following mouseover (relatedTarget <a>) is ignored at :382. Bootstrap keeps the tip shown. A delegated child entered over its SVG icon opens nothing in the engine. No row and no case.
behaviors.claim: Tip.#handleTrigger and #resolveContext must treat any Node relatedTarget or target, SVG included, as Bootstrap does (src/browser/Tip.ts:348-387).

behaviors.title: leave during the show transition hides after shown

questions: The Orchestrator must rule on toggleEnabled. guide/veneer.md:616 says the engine serves Bootstrap's plugin methods, but TooltipInterface (guide/veneer.md:444-455) has no toggleEnabled, and the rename of dispose to destroy and setContent to write appears only in the Methods section. Do these API differences need departure rows, or must line 616 name the vocabulary change?

Error class and message differ with no departure row. Bootstrap throws Error('Please use show on visible elements'), and its spec at tooltip.spec.js:674 asserts that message. The engine throws VeneerError TIP_HIDDEN with 'Use show on visible elements' (src/browser/Tip.ts:153). Only the Methods table records this (guide/veneer.md:449).

Replacement of a markup-built lifetime has no departure row. The factory rule at guide/veneer.md:622 replaces it when options are passed, where Bootstrap's getOrCreateInstance returns the existing instance and ignores the config. Must this be a row?

Bootstrap's documented way to extend the allowlist is to mutate Tooltip.Default.allowList, which sanitizer.spec.js:100 shows. The engine freezes HTML_ALLOWLIST (src/browser/constants.ts:196) and accepts only a per-instance sanitize.allowlist. Is that a contract refusal that the guide must state?

Attacked and held: delegated triggers listen in the capture phase (src/browser/Tip.ts:84, :94), and Bootstrap does the same, because addHandler passes isDelegated as useCapture (js/src/dom/event-handler.js:184). This is not a difference.

results.contract: The engine serves Bootstrap 5.3.8's tab data API, meaning clicks on [data-bs-toggle="tab"|"pill"|"list"] with anchor and AREA prevention and refusal of disabled toggles (plugins.ts:313-331). It also serves load-time boot of active toggles, show and destroy through createTab and Registry.component, and the show, shown, hide, and hidden .bs.tab events from Bootstrap's own hosts; the guide states this at /home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:616-622, 634-636, and 650. The tab-specific departures are the tab-destroy and tab-destroyed rows at veneer.md:873-898; the shared rows transition-wait (veneer.md:743) and event-detail (veneer.md:742) also apply.

results.contract: The engine serves Bootstrap 5.3.8's toast on Bootstrap's markup through four parts: the `[data-bs-dismiss="toast"]` click route (plugins.ts:339-353), `createToast` returning the host's live `ToastInterface` with `show`, `hide`, and `destroy` plus `visible` and `phase`, the four `*.bs.toast` events as cancelable bubbling `ComponentEvent` values, and options grouped as `animation` and `dismiss.automatic`/`dismiss.delay`. The guide states these in the Browser entry chapter at /home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:616, :622, :634, :636, and :638, summarizes the toast proofs at :648, and has only one toast-specific departure row (`mistyped-input`, :739); the generic rows at :742-745 also apply to the toast.

behaviors.title: VERSION: should return plugin version
behaviors.evidence: Bootstrap's class-static metadata (base-component.js:69-71). The engine exports no VERSION, and the guide's JS surface is the factory API (guides/veneer.md:622) plus the ComponentInterface vocabulary (:634). No refusal names it explicitly; see questions.

verdicts.title: close() on a disposed or completed alert: Bootstrap throws a TypeError on the nulled element; the engine does nothing
verdicts.evidence: Lane: objective. Bootstrap behavior: dispose() nulls every own property (base-component.js:43-45). EventHandler.trigger(null, ...) returns null (dom/event-handler.js:259-261), so `closeEvent.defaultPrevented` at alert.js:40 throws a TypeError. The engine returns at /home/user/veneer/src/browser/Alert.ts:50. Nothing pins the difference. /home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Alert.test.ts:190 calls close() after destroy, runs only in the engine realm, and asserts nothing after the call. Deleting Alert.ts:50 would still pass, because show is already gone and the transcript is already taken. The guide states the engine's intent at /home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:634 ('the mutating methods do nothing'). No row in /home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:722-988 records Bootstrap's error, unlike the precedent rows alert-destroy (:747) and dropdown:focus-destroy (:737). Graded gap because the DOM is identical and only the uncaught-error count differs, and the engine side is the stated contract. Required change: add a supplemental `$::errors` row (Bootstrap 1, engine 0) under a new alert scenario, for example alert-closed. Consume it in an Alert.test.ts case that completes a close in both realms, calls close on the oracle's stale instance and on the engine alert, and records native error counts the way Alert.test.ts:207-259 does.

verdicts.title: A second close during the fade queues a second callback; Bootstrap's second callback throws on the disposed host
verdicts.evidence: Lane: objective. In Bootstrap, the second click reaches the same live instance (component-functions.js:26, base-component.js:65-66) and dispatches a second close.bs.alert (alert.js:38). It then queues a second transitionend handler (util/index.js:240-250). On the transitionend, handler 1 runs _destroyElement and dispose (alert.js:51-55). Handler 2 then calls `this._element.remove()` on null and throws a TypeError. In the engine, the second route finds the live Alert (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/helpers.ts:103-108) and dispatches a second close.bs.alert (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/Alert.ts:51). It adds a second pending wait (Alert.ts:54-56), which destroy aborts (Alert.ts:64), so #complete returns at Alert.ts:72. Events and DOM agree, and only the error count differs (Bootstrap 1, engine 0). No case in /home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Alert.test.ts:82-343 drives two closes before completion. No row beyond alert-destroy and alert-reduced (/home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:747-748) covers it. Required change: add an oracle case in Alert.test.ts that clicks the dismiss button twice inside a slowed fade in both realms. It compares transcripts (two close.bs.alert, one closed.bs.alert) and consumes a new `$::errors` row (1 against 0) through the ledger, with the delete-row and wrong-value controls of Alert.test.ts:257-259.

verdicts.title: A close.bs.alert listener that disposes the instance: Bootstrap throws at classList on the nulled element; the engine returns quietly
verdicts.evidence: Lane: objective. In Bootstrap, a close.bs.alert listener calling Alert.getInstance(el).dispose() nulls _element (base-component.js:43-45). After the listener returns, closeEvent.defaultPrevented is false (alert.js:40), and `this._element.classList` at alert.js:44 throws a TypeError. The alert keeps class show. In the engine, the post-dispatch check `|| this.destroyed` at /home/user/veneer/src/browser/Alert.ts:51 returns quietly, and the alert also keeps show. DOM and events agree, and the error count differs. No Alert.test.ts case destroys inside the close hook (/home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Alert.test.ts:82-343), and no row covers it (/home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:722-988). Mutation check: deleting `|| this.destroyed` at Alert.ts:51 would remove show from a destroyed alert, and no current test would fail. Required change: add an oracle case whose close listener disposes (Bootstrap) or destroys (engine). Assert identical transcripts (show retained, no closed.bs.alert) and consume a `$::errors` row (1 against 0).

verdicts.title: Dismiss delegation phase: Bootstrap listens in the document bubble phase, the engine in the document capture phase
verdicts.evidence: The claim's premise is false. Bootstrap's delegated handlers also listen in the capture phase. component-functions.js:16 passes a selector string as the handler argument, so normalizeParameters sets isDelegated = true (dom/event-handler.js:130). addHandler then registers `element.addEventListener(typeEvent, fn, isDelegated)` (dom/event-handler.js:184), which makes document click.dismiss.bs.alert a capture-phase listener. The engine also listens on the document in the capture phase (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/Veneer.ts:70-73). Consequently, stopPropagation on the trigger or an ancestor blocks dismissal in neither realm, and close.bs.alert precedes the trigger's own click listeners in both. The phases match, so no departure row is owed. A capture listener on the document that a page registers before the engine might still run in a different order relative to the engine, because the engine registers at createVeneer and Bootstrap at module load. That ordering is a separate question, and the claim does not raise it.

verdicts.title: Orphan or unresolvable dismiss trigger: Bootstrap throws (TypeError on a null instance, or SyntaxError on an invalid selector); the engine does nothing or falls back to the closest .alert
verdicts.evidence: Lane: objective. The claim covers three cases. (a) Invalid data-bs-target with an .alert ancestor: Bootstrap's getElementFromSelector calls querySelector on the invalid selector (dom/selector-engine.js:113-116, :32, :40-41). That throws a SyntaxError inside the delegated listener before `|| this.closest('.alert')` (component-functions.js:25) is evaluated, so the alert stays. The engine catches the error and returns [] (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/helpers.ts:715-723). resolveDismiss then falls back to the ancestor (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/helpers.ts:186-188), and the route closes it (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/plugins.ts:43-44). The DOM differs (alert removed against alert kept), so this case is a defect. (b) No target, or an unmatched valid target, and no ancestor: Bootstrap's getOrCreateInstance(null) builds an element-less instance (base-component.js:27-30, :65-66). Its close() reads defaultPrevented on the null from EventHandler.trigger (dom/event-handler.js:259-261, alert.js:40) and throws a TypeError. The engine resolves no host (helpers.ts:188) and does nothing. Only the error count differs. (c) A valid unmatched target with an ancestor falls back to the ancestor in both realms (component-functions.js:25, helpers.ts:186-188), so it is not a difference. Nothing pins (a) or (b): /home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/helpers.test.ts:377-402 tests only a valid matched target and an ancestor fallback, and no row appears in /home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:722-988. The same resolveDismiss path serves modal, offcanvas, and toast (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/plugins.ts:225, :265, :349), so refer the cross-family fix to the Orchestrator. Required change at /home/user/veneer/src/browser/helpers.ts:184-188: when data-bs-target or href yields a selector that fails to parse, resolve no host instead of falling back to closest(selector), which matches Bootstrap's outcome of the alert kept. Alternatively, record a departure row. Pin (a) with an oracle case in Alert.test.ts using data-bs-target="[" inside an .alert, and record (b)'s error count as a `$::errors` row with a proof.

verdicts.title: A toggle inserted after the data API is live toggles on click (selector resolved at event time)
verdicts.evidence: The behavior belongs to the shared router, and a proof the reader cites already covers that router. The button plugin has no boot entry and no state of its own: it is a single delegated click route (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/plugins.ts:56-68). Every route goes through the same code that matches the selector when the event fires (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/Veneer.ts:186-204) and through buildPlugin's route wrapper (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/helpers.ts:87-113). Neither keeps a set of hosts captured at boot. /home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Veneer.test.ts:497-523 creates the scope first, then appends a trigger and clicks it, so it pins event-time selector resolution on that shared path. A mutation that resolves selectors at boot would have to go into Veneer.#route or buildPlugin, and that case would fail. A mutation local to the button family (its selector, prevent, or execute) would also break the existing pre-boot button cases at /home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Button.test.ts:113-166 and /home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Veneer.test.ts:913-915. Bootstrap also delegates from document and runs querySelectorAll on every event (event-handler.js:104), so the two engines do not differ. A button-specific case would add coverage but no new discriminating power.

results.contract: The engine runs Bootstrap 5.3.8's data API, plugin methods, and `*.bs.*` events on Bootstrap's own markup. A page opts in through `createVeneer(root, { plugins: createBootstrapPlugins() })`. Components live in a document registry keyed by host and plugin and are reached through typed factories. The shared mechanics (markup input parsing, target resolution, transition waits, event dispatch, and the dismiss routes) are stated at /home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:616-640. Every deliberate difference is a row of the "Engine departures" table at /home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:716-988. The table's preamble at :718 limits it to identical markup, so the shape of Bootstrap's class and static JS API falls outside it.

verdicts.title: constructor: should ignore keyboard events if data-bs-keyboard=false
verdicts.evidence: Engine gate at /home/user/veneer/src/browser/Carousel.ts:72; projection at /home/user/veneer/src/browser/helpers.ts:313. The only carousel keyboard option evidence is the bad-value default at /home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/helpers.test.ts:690-699. The app's carousel scenarios carry no keyboard option (/home/user/veneer/tests/setupBrowser.ts:2641-2707). Mutation: ignoring options.keyboard at Carousel.ts:72 fails no case. The scenario sets data-bs-keyboard="false" on both hosts, sends an ArrowRight key step, and expects zero slide events with matching 'prevented' readings.

verdicts.evidence: The oracle keyboard case sends only arrows and editable-target keys (/home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Carousel.test.ts:478-483). The app scenario's {Escape} door (/home/user/veneer/tests/setupBrowser.ts:2692, 2618-2626) pins only the absence of slide events, engine-only, and reads no defaultPrevented. Required change: add { action: 'key', selector: '#carousel', key: 'ArrowDown' } to the keyboard case at Carousel.test.ts:478-483. verdicts.title: constructor: should not slide if arrow key is pressed and carousel is sliding
verdicts.evidence: Both arrow steps wait for slid (/home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Carousel.test.ts:479-480). No other case sends a key during a pending slide. Bootstrap's guard is carousel.js:301-303; the engine's is /home/user/veneer/src/browser/Carousel.ts:238. The spec forces _isSliding, a Bootstrap-internal field, but a second key press during a slide is a page-observable behavior, so the behavior is in contract. Mutation: dropping `this.sliding` at Carousel.ts:238 leaves the keyboard path unguarded and fails no case. Required change: add a key step without `until`, followed by a second arrow step, to Carousel.test.ts:478-483. Both realms then record a single slide event.

It dispatches touchstart, touchmove, and touchend with a +300 px displacement and compares the slide direction 'right' and the prev item.

verdicts.title: next: should not slide if the carousel is sliding
verdicts.evidence: Every method step waits for slid (/home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Carousel.test.ts:449-462). The engine-only destroy case calls next then select (Carousel.test.ts:234-235), which exercises select's own queue at /home/user/veneer/src/browser/Carousel.ts:154 and not the next guard. The case then expects one additional slide event, not two.

verdicts.title: next: should update the active element to the next item before sliding
verdicts.evidence: _activeElement is Bootstrap-internal (carousel.js:342). Its page-observable consequence is that _updateInterval reads it (carousel.js:289) on the restart at carousel.js:367-368, and the engine mirrors that at /home/user/veneer/src/browser/Carousel.ts:168-169, 296. The 'interval' scenario puts data-bs-interval only on the active item and pauses at the first slid (/home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Carousel.test.ts:514-520, 599-601). The restarted interval is therefore never observed. Mutation: dropping `#pending?.next` at Carousel.ts:169 restarts at 20 ms instead of 1000 ms and fails no case. Required change: give the second item data-bs-interval in a cycling scenario that observes the second timer slide's timing window in both realms.

verdicts.title: next: should continue cycling if it was already
verdicts.evidence: Every cycling path pauses at the first slid: the load case (/home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Carousel.test.ts:127-129, 137-141), 'interval' and 'hover disabled' (Carousel.test.ts:599-601), and 'interaction' (pause on every slid, 599-601). In 'touch hold' the end callback pauses after the slide (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/Carousel.ts:102-104). Mutation: deleting `if (cycling) this.start()` at Carousel.ts:296 fails no case. Required change: add a cycling scenario with no slid pause that waits for two timer slides in both realms. The engine's cycling getter must also report true while the first slide is pending.

verdicts.title: prev: should not slide if the carousel is sliding
verdicts.evidence: The prev step waits for slid (/home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Carousel.test.ts:451). The guards at /home/user/veneer/src/browser/Carousel.ts:146 and :238 are unexercised. verdicts.title: cycle: should clear interval if there is one
verdicts.evidence: No path calls start() while a timer is live. The direct case starts once and then pauses (/home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Carousel.test.ts:199-202). Required change: add a case that calls cycle twice in both realms, pauses, waits a window longer than the interval, and expects zero slid events. With an orphaned timer the engine keeps sliding.

verdicts.title: source: Swipe.dispose leaves the pointer-event class on the host
verdicts.evidence: Bootstrap's dispose only calls EventHandler.off (swipe.js:73-75), so the class added at swipe.js:128 stays. The engine releases the class through Hold (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/Swipe.ts:78-82, 46-47), and the guide documents this only in prose (/home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:345, 662). The departure table has no row for it: its carousel rows 904-942 come from the non-touch case at /home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Carousel.test.ts:260-356, and the only touch rows are touch-ownership at guides/veneer.md:726-727. The engine-only pins are Carousel.test.ts:252 and Swipe.test.ts:24, 62. Engine behavior is the documented contract; the required change is a departure row. Run the carousel-destroy transcript under touch emulation, or add a touch destroy case, and add a row such as `carousel-destroy-touch | $/div[1]::class | ["carousel","pointer-event","slide"] | ["carousel","slide"]` consumed by that case.

verdicts.title: source: dispose leaves image dragstart listeners live
verdicts.evidence: Bootstrap registers dragstart.bs.carousel on each img (carousel.js:220-222). dispose calls EventHandler.off(this._element, '.bs.carousel') (base-component.js:41), which reaches only the host's handler registry, so the image handlers stay live. The engine aborts them with the lifetime signal (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/Carousel.ts:98, 198). The only pin is engine-only (/home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Carousel.test.ts:226, 253), and no departure row exists (/home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:904-942). Required change: add a supplemental $::dragstart-prevented reading to a touch-emulated destroy comparison, plus a row recording Bootstrap 'true' and engine 'false'.

verdicts.title: source: dispose leaves the touch timeout live, which throws from the nulled _config
verdicts.evidence: Bootstrap nulls every own property on dispose (base-component.js:43-45) but never clears touchTimeout. The timeout calls _maybeEnableCycle (carousel.js:242), which reads this._config.ride (carousel.js:157) on null and throws a TypeError. The engine clears the timeout (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/Carousel.ts:200), and resume() also returns once destroyed (:187). The only proof is engine-only, with no oracle and no error reading (/home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Carousel.test.ts:228-233, 238, 247-252). Row 744 (transition-abort) covers transition callbacks only, not timeouts (/home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:744). Required change: add an oracle comparison that ends a touch on both hosts, disposes within 500 ms plus interval, waits past the timeout, and records a $::errors reading. Add a row with Bootstrap 1 and engine 0.

verdicts.title: source: pending completion after dispose throws in Bootstrap

verdicts.title: activate: if configured not to autofocus, should not autofocus itself

verdicts.title: Dialog compensation reads the scrollbar width after the body lock
verdicts.evidence: Bootstrap's show() runs _scrollBar.hide() (modal.js:114) before _adjustDialog (modal.js:118). _adjustDialog calls getWidth() fresh (modal.js:298), after body overflow:hidden has propagated to the viewport, so the width is 0. A short modal then gets no padding, and a tall modal gets paddingLeft '0px'. The engine's update (Modal.ts:147-157) reads Lock.width, which returns the stored pre-lock measurement while locked (Lock.ts:30-33, stored at 59 and 88). On a page with a classic scrollbar, the engine therefore writes paddingRight = W px on a short modal and nothing on a tall one. The resize path (Modal.ts:79-85) repeats the difference. No departure row covers it (guides/veneer.md:716-919). All Modal.test.ts:286 fixtures run with the body emptied (Modal.test.ts:430-438), so both realms measure 0. Fix at Modal.ts:151: measure Math.abs(innerWidth - documentElement.clientWidth) at call time instead of reading this.#lock.width. Pinning probe: a 'page scrollbar' scenario that adds tall body content to both realms, opens a short modal and a tall modal, and compares #modal::style.

verdicts.title: RTL swaps the compensation side

No modal case sets dir on documentElement; a grep for rtl and dir in Modal.test.ts finds none. Mutation: swap paddingLeft and paddingRight in either branch. Nothing turns red. Required proof: the 'overflow' scenario run under dir=rtl in both realms.

verdicts.title: A prevented hidePrevented event skips the static bounce
verdicts.evidence: Modal.ts:233 returns on defaultPrevented. 'O2 writes nothing after destruction from hidePrevented' (Modal.test.ts:87-109) destroys from the listener, so the separate `if (this.destroyed) return` at Modal.ts:234 also stops it. Mutation: drop `.defaultPrevented` from line 233. Nothing turns red. The veto scenarios cover show and hide only (Modal.test.ts:394-398, 439-443). Required proof: preventDefault on hidePrevented.bs.modal for a static modal. Compare against the oracle: no modal-static class, no overflowY write, and no focus move.

verdicts.title: show is accepted during the backdrop fade-out after _hideModal
verdicts.evidence: Bootstrap clears _isTransitioning in _hideModal (modal.js:250) before backdrop.hide (252). A show() during the backdrop fade therefore passes the guard at modal.js:99 and emits show.bs.modal. The engine keeps #hiding until the end of #close (Modal.ts:228), so show() returns at Modal.ts:117 without emitting show.bs.modal. That is an observable event difference on identical markup. No departure row covers it (guides/veneer.md:716-919). The overlap case runs with transitions off (Modal.test.ts:328-331), so the window never opens. Recommended path: add a departure row with a proof, because Bootstrap's accepted show is later undone by the stale backdrop callback (modal.js:252-256 removes modal-open and resets the lock). It closes with a second click. Clearing #active.click on mouseout must make that scenario fail.

The factory case calls show twice but never hide while hidden (/home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/factories.test.ts:203-213). verdicts.evidence: The `#trap.deactivate()` call at /home/user/veneer/src/browser/Offcanvas.ts:135 and the `#trap.destroy()` call at :156 can both be removed without a failure. After hide or destroy, every single-panel case leaves the panel `visibility:hidden`. verdicts.title: data-api: should not prevent event for input
verdicts.evidence: The engine's behavior matches Bootstrap by source. The offcanvas toggle route has no `prevent` (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/plugins.ts:244-259). The fallback prevents only on A or AREA (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/helpers.ts:94-98), matching offcanvas.js:235-237. Nothing pins it for this route. /home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/plugins.test.ts:44-57 drives the offcanvas route only with an anchor trigger and asserts `defaultPrevented` true. No offcanvas case uses an INPUT trigger: the only checkbox hits are the app form at /home/user/veneer/tests/app/browser/integration.test.ts:565-577. The native `click` is absent from ORACLE_EVENTS (/home/user/veneer/tests/setupBrowser.ts:4110-4185), whose listeners bind literal names (:4832). A <button> opener's prevented click is invisible, so `prevent: () => true` on plugins.ts:244 fails no case. verdicts.title: Re-show while hiding (close, then reopen within the transition)
verdicts.evidence: The engine's end state differs from Bootstrap's. In the engine, `show()` during `#hiding` passes `visible` (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/Offcanvas.ts:97, :116). `#lock.acquire()` is then a no-op for the owner that still holds the lock (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/Lock.ts:46). `Backdrop.show` aborts the pending removal (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/Backdrop.ts:38, :72-73). Only `destroy` aborts the stale `#close` (Offcanvas.ts:180), which strips aria-modal and role and releases the lock (:186-188). The engine ends with `show`, no aria-modal, an unlocked body, and a live `.offcanvas-backdrop`. Its `visible` is false (:94-101), so Escape, a backdrop click, and dismiss all return at :133 and leave the backdrop on the page. Bootstrap sets `_isShown = true` (offcanvas.js:104) and re-saves overflow 'hidden' to data-bs-overflow (scrollbar.js:60, :79-83). Its hide completion restores 'hidden' (:86-96), so the body stays locked. Its pending backdrop dispose still runs (backdrop.js:91-95, :99-107), and Escape still closes (offcanvas.js:129, :201-203). No departure row covers this (/home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:728-735, :845-858). The 'overlap' scenario drives hide during show, not show during hide (/home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Offcanvas.test.ts:307-308, :346-347). Fix Offcanvas.ts so a superseding `show()` cancels the pending `#close` completion, or add departure rows. Either way, pin it with an oracle scenario: click #opener until shown, click `.btn-close`, click #opener before `hidden.bs.offcanvas`, wait for `shown.bs.offcanvas`, then press Escape on #offcanvas. Read the body style, backdrop nodes, and events.

verdicts.title: Markup `.offcanvas.show` that already carries aria-modal is shown at load
verdicts.evidence: Bootstrap starts every instance with `_isShown = false` (offcanvas.js:69). Its load handler calls `show()` on each `.offcanvas.show` (:260-263), which runs the full open (:93-125). The engine reads `visible` from the `show` class plus aria-modal (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/Offcanvas.ts:94-101). verdicts.title: show() on a toggle with no tablist parent
verdicts.evidence: Bootstrap: with _parent null, show() calls _getActiveElem, then _getChildren, then SelectorEngine.find(SELECTOR_INNER_ELEM, null) (tab.js:87, 184, 180). The default parameter at selector-engine.js:36 covers only undefined, so Element.prototype.querySelectorAll.call(null, …) at selector-engine.js:37 throws a TypeError before any event or write. Through the data API (tab.js:289-299) the delegated handler throws and the markup stays unchanged. Engine: /home/user/veneer/src/browser/Tab.ts:118 returns [] for a null parent. show() then emits show.bs.tab with relatedTarget null (Tab.ts:100) and adds .active to the toggle and its pane (Tab.ts:134-135). Because the constructor returned before writing role (Tab.ts:37), #activated adds .show to the toggle and dispatches no shown event (Tab.ts:159-161). No departure row covers this (/home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:873-898 hold only tab-destroy and tab-destroyed rows). The guide records a similar Bootstrap throw as the dropdown:focus-destroy row at veneer.md:737. The plugin route reaches it on markup alone (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/plugins.ts:321-323). Required change: at Tab.ts:92-93, make show() refuse with no event and no write when #parent is not an element. Otherwise add a tab-orphan row to the departure table at veneer.md:716-898 that records Bootstrap's $::errors TypeError against the engine's event and class writes, and have an oracle case in Tab.test.ts consume it.

verdicts.title: Default: should expose default setting to allow to override them
verdicts.evidence: Lane: objective. Upheld. Bootstrap returns the mutable module object from Toast.Default (js/src/toast.js:41-45, :62-64), so a page assignment changes every later construction. The engine freezes TOAST_DEFAULTS (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/constants.ts:145), and resolveToastOptions reads only that object (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/helpers.ts:421-428). No test assigns or reads an overridden default. The guide gives TOAST_DEFAULTS one line (/home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:69). The contract at veneer.md:616 lists what the engine serves (the data API, plugin methods, and *.bs.* events) and never says it refuses class statics such as Default, DefaultType, NAME, or getInstance. The departure table (veneer.md:720-988) has no toast row and no row for statics. Silence in a list of served surfaces is not a stated refusal, so the claim stands. Required change at veneer.md:616 or :638: add a sentence that refuses Bootstrap's class statics and global default mutation, and point to typed factory options as the path. The alternative is an overridable defaults seam in helpers.ts:421; the guide sentence is the cheaper fix and matches the freeze.

verdicts.title: show: should not trigger shown if show is prevented
verdicts.evidence: Upheld. The engine returns on veto at /home/user/veneer/src/browser/Toast.ts:65. verdicts.title: show: should clear timeout if toast is shown again before it is hidden
verdicts.evidence: Upheld. 'matches repeated show' (/home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Toast.test.ts:215-224) passes no automatic argument, so it runs with compareToast's default automatic=false (:50) and no timer exists. The only other re-show with a timer is step 3 of the focus case (Toast.test.ts:192). verdicts.title: show: should clear timeout if toast is interacted with mouse

Deleting the clear at /home/user/veneer/src/browser/Toast.ts:149 changes no reading in this case. verdicts.title: show: should clear timeout if toast is interacted with keyboard
verdicts.evidence: Upheld. verdicts.title: Orphan [data-bs-dismiss="toast"] with no target and no .toast ancestor: Bootstrap throws TypeError from a host-less instance; the engine is inert
verdicts.evidence: Upheld as an undeclared departure. In Bootstrap, getElementFromSelector and closest('.toast') both return null (component-functions.js:25). getOrCreateInstance(null) then builds a host-less Toast, because BaseComponent returns before assigning _element (base-component.js:27-30, :65-67). Toast's listener setup skips the null element. Then hide() reads this._element.classList at toast.js:103/:134 and throws a TypeError out of the document click listener, which the page sees as an error event. In the engine, resolveDismiss returns [] (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/helpers.ts:184-189), the toast route has no gate (/home/user/veneer/src/browser/plugins.ts:345-351), and the loop at helpers.ts:101 does nothing, so no error is reported. Anchor prevention still matches Bootstrap, because helpers.ts:93-98 prevents the default before the empty host loop. No test builds an orphan trigger: helpers.test.ts:377-387 tests resolveDismiss only with a host present, and plugins.test.ts:45-66 always supplies data-bs-target. The guide says the table records every deliberate difference (/home/user/veneer/guides/veneer.md:718), but no row covers this one; the closest analogues are alert-destroy (:747) and dropdown:focus-destroy (:737). Required change: add a 'toast:orphan-dismiss' row at the $::errors path (Bootstrap 1, Engine 0, citing component-functions.js:25 and toast.js:103). Add an oracle case in /home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Toast.test.ts that clicks an orphan [data-bs-dismiss="toast"] in both realms and consumes that row through the native error recorder the alert proof uses. The same route shape applies to the alert dismiss (plugins.ts:42 area); refer that to the alert family.

verdicts.title: getDataAttributes: should get only bs-prefixed data attributes without bs namespace
verdicts.evidence: The engine matches Bootstrap: /home/user/veneer/src/browser/parsers.ts:35 filters with key.startsWith('bs') && !key.startsWith('bsConfig'). The only parseAttributes fixture is /home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/helpers.test.ts:669-685, and it carries data-bs-* attributes plus data-bs-config-extra. That last one tests the bsConfig exclusion, not a key without the bs prefix. No departure row covers this. The risk is lower than the claim says: with the filter removed, key.slice(2) mangles names, so data-backdrop becomes 'ckdrop' and still never reaches 'backdrop'. Only a collision such as data-xxkeyboard would leak into options. Fix: in helpers.test.ts:669, add data-another, data-target-bs, data-in-bs-out, and data-xxkeyboard to the host and assert that parseAttributes(host) equals exactly the bs-derived keys, matching manipulator.spec.js:63-71.

verdicts.title: getElementFromSelector: should get element from href if no data-bs-target set

verdicts.title: isVisible: should return true if its a closed details element

verdicts.title: isDisabled: should return true if the element has disabled attribute
verdicts.evidence: /home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/validators.test.ts:70-71 asserts only disabled="false" on a summary. Every family fixture that disables a non-form element uses the class: /home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Tab.test.ts:105, /home/user/veneer/tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts:31, and /home/user/veneer/tests/setupBrowser.ts:4323 (grep for `<(a|div|span|li)[^>]* disabled`).
